description:
Every wrapper (verify_tls_server, verify_tls_client_*, verify_smime_*, verify_code_signer, verify_time_stamper, verify_ocsp_responder) calls verify_chain internally. verify_chain dispatches into Verifier::verify_one, which can return ANY Error variant including:

- Error::Aia(AiaError)            — AIA fetch failed during slow-path reassembly
- Error::PathBuild(pkix_path_builder::Error)  — path-builder ran out of candidates
- Error::AiaDepthExceeded         — AIA recursion cap reached

But the wrapper rustdocs list only:

- verify_tls_server (lines 743-750): Error::Path, Error::Revocation, Error::Identity
- verify_tls_client_dns (lines 827-835): Error::Path, Error::Revocation, Error::Identity
- verify_tls_client_mailbox (lines 904-912): Error::Path, Error::Revocation, Error::Identity
- verify_smime_signer (lines 974-981): Error::Path, Error::Revocation, Error::Identity
- verify_smime_recipient (lines 1007-1014): inherits via "Identical mechanics" cross-reference
- verify_code_signer (lines 1061-1066): Error::Path, Error::Revocation
- verify_time_stamper (lines 1127-1136): Error::Path, Error::Revocation, Error::ProfileViolation
- verify_ocsp_responder (lines 1236-1249): Error::Path, Error::Revocation, Error::OcspDelegation

The wrappers ALL bake `&NoAiaFetcher` so they cannot in practice return Error::Aia(non-FetchingDisabled) — but the doc-level guarantee is missing. The caller seeing:

    match verify_tls_server(...) {
        Err(Error::Path(_)) => ...
        Err(Error::Revocation(_)) => ...
        Err(Error::Identity(_)) => ...
        // exhaustive match impossible because Error is #[non_exhaustive]
    }

…cannot tell from the rustdoc whether Error::Aia is reachable. They have to read the source to find out it's gated by &NoAiaFetcher being passed through, AND that NoAiaFetcher returns Error::Aia(AiaError::FetchingDisabled) on any orphaned chain.

Concretely, today a caller invokes `verify_tls_server(&[leaf_only], ...)` with an intentionally-incomplete chain expecting a clean error. They get `Error::Aia(AiaError::FetchingDisabled)`. The wrapper's Errors section does not warn them this is possible.

WHY IT MATTERS:

The slash-command checklist for underspecified contracts calls out:

> Error behavior that is undocumented or inconsistent with the rest of the crate. A caller cannot write defensive code if they cannot tell from the signature or docs which errors are possible.

That is exactly what happened here. Three credible fixes:

(a) **Document Aia/PathBuild/AiaDepthExceeded in every wrapper's Errors section** with the qualifier "but only when the supplied chain has a break — the wrapper's hardcoded NoAiaFetcher makes this surface as Error::Aia(FetchingDisabled)."

(b) **Translate Error::Aia(FetchingDisabled) into a wrapper-friendly variant** at the wrapper boundary. E.g., have wrappers return Error::Path(pkix_path::Error::ChainBroken { index }) when the inner error is FetchingDisabled. Hides the AIA-implementation detail from wrappers that don't expose AIA to the caller.

(c) **Catalog the full possible error set** in a crate-level rustdoc table mapping each wrapper to its possible error variants, then cross-reference. Replaces per-wrapper Errors sections with one source of truth.

This is closely related to PKIX-sqek.4 (wrappers can't opt into AIA): if (b) is chosen alongside the PKIX-sqek.4 fix (wrappers grow generic over AiaFetcher = NoAiaFetcher), the documented Errors sections gain Error::Aia variants conditionally, matching what the wrapper can actually return.

Filed as P2 because the contract gap is a real footgun for defensive callers (especially those using match exhaustiveness), but downstream consumers can always pattern-match on Error::* and a fallback `_` arm — it doesn't cause incorrect validation, just confused error handling.
title: Wrappers omit Error::Aia / Error::PathBuild / Error::AiaDepthExceeded from their documented Errors lists
